blocks.raw: # Tier Upgrade
blocks.text: Tier Upgrade

blocks.raw: A tier upgrade moves a customer from their current tier within a [loyalty program](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-a-multi-loyalty-program) to a higher tier which could have more benefits & incentives. Customers receive a tier upgrade when they meet specific eligibility criteria set within the tier configurations or sometimes via workflows (using upgrade-to-tier action).
blocks.text: A tier upgrade moves a customer from their current tier within a loyalty program to a higher tier which could have more benefits & incentives. Customers receive a tier upgrade when they meet specific eligibility criteria set within the tier configurations or sometimes via workflows (using upgrade-to-tier action).

blocks.raw:
> 📘 Note
>
> Tier upgrades for a loyalty program can be configured in the advanced settings of the program. Refer to the documentation on [advanced settings](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/loyalty-org-settingsdf) for more information.
blocks.text: NoteTier upgrades for a loyalty program can be configured in the advanced settings of the program. Refer to the documentation on advanced settings for more information.

blocks.raw: # Eligibility criteria
blocks.text: Eligibility criteria

blocks.raw: You can configure tier upgrades for both individual customers and user groups. For user groups, you must explicitly configure the SlabUpgrade activity for the User Group entity. Group-based tier upgrades use group-level tracker values, such as total group spend, to determine eligibility. Refer to the trackers section below for details on configuring group-level criteria.

Group-based tier upgrades use group-level tracker values, such as total group spend, to determine eligibility. Refer to the trackers section below for details on configuring group-level criteria.

blocks.raw: A customer can receive a tier upgrade by meeting the eligibility criteria set in the program. The following are the criteria available currently for a tier upgrade:
blocks.text: A customer can receive a tier upgrade by meeting the eligibility criteria set in the program. The following are the criteria available currently for a tier upgrade:

blocks.raw: ## 1. Current points
blocks.text: 1. Current points

blocks.raw: Current points are the active points that a customer has at present. The customer must meet a certain threshold of points set by the loyalty program to qualify for the upgrade.
blocks.text: Current points are the active points that a customer has at present. The customer must meet a certain threshold of points set by the loyalty program to qualify for the upgrade.

blocks.raw: ### Example
blocks.text: Example

blocks.raw: Consider the following case:
blocks.text: Consider the following case:

blocks.raw:
* Upgrade eligibility from a base tier to a higher tier: **1000 points**
* The points the customer holds at present: **900 points**
blocks.text: Upgrade eligibility from a base tier to a higher tier: 1000 pointsThe points the customer holds at present: 900 points

blocks.raw: In this case, the customer must earn **100 more active points** to meet the criteria for upgrading the tier. When the customer meets the eligibility criteria of **1000 points**, they are upgraded to the higher tier.
blocks.text: In this case, the customer must earn 100 more active points to meet the criteria for upgrading the tier. When the customer meets the eligibility criteria of 1000 points, they are upgraded to the higher tier.

blocks.raw: ## 2. Lifetime points
blocks.text: 2. Lifetime points

blocks.raw: Lifetime points are the total points a customer has earned throughout their journey in the program. These include active, expired, and redeemed points. The customer must meet a certain threshold of lifetime points set by the loyalty program to qualify for the upgrade.
blocks.text: Lifetime points are the total points a customer has earned throughout their journey in the program. These include active, expired, and redeemed points. The customer must meet a certain threshold of lifetime points set by the loyalty program to qualify for the upgrade.

blocks.raw: ### Example

blocks.raw: Consider the following case:
blocks.text: Consider the following case:

blocks.raw:
* Upgrade eligibility from a base tier to a higher tier: **5000 lifetime points**
* Total lifetime points customer earned: **3500 points**
blocks.text: Upgrade eligibility from a base tier to a higher tier: 5000 lifetime pointsTotal lifetime points customer earned: 3500 points

blocks.raw: In this case, the customer must earn **1500 more points** to meet the eligibility criteria. When the customer reaches **5000 lifetime points**, they are upgraded to the higher tier.
blocks.text: In this case, the customer must earn 1500 more points to meet the eligibility criteria. When the customer reaches 5000 lifetime points, they are upgraded to the higher tier.

blocks.raw: ## 3. Lifetime purchases
blocks.text: 3. Lifetime purchases

blocks.raw: Lifetime purchases are the total amount a customer has spent throughout their journey in the program. The customer must meet a certain threshold of lifetime purchases set by the loyalty program to qualify for the upgrade.
blocks.text: Lifetime purchases are the total amount a customer has spent throughout their journey in the program. The customer must meet a certain threshold of lifetime purchases set by the loyalty program to qualify for the upgrade.

blocks.raw: ### Example
blocks.text: Example

blocks.raw: Consider the following case:

* Upgrade eligibility from a base tier to a higher tier: **$5000 lifetime purchases**
* Total lifetime purchases of the customer: **$4000**
blocks.text: Upgrade eligibility from a base tier to a higher tier: $5000 lifetime purchasesTotal lifetime purchases of the customer: $4000

blocks.raw: In this case, the customer has to make a purchase of at least **$1000** to meet the eligibility criteria. When the customer reaches $5,000 in spending, they are upgraded to the higher tier.
blocks.text: In this case, the customer has to make a purchase of at least $1000 to meet the eligibility criteria. When the customer reaches $5,000 in spending, they are upgraded to the higher tier.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 **Note**
>
> Tier upgrades based on lifetime spend or points are evaluated in the order transactions actually happened, not the order they were processed. If a backdated transaction is processed after a later transaction has already been evaluated, its value is not retroactively considered for the tracker aggregate used for that slab evaluation and the customer's tier may not reflect their true lifetime total until a subsequent transaction re-triggers evaluation.

blocks.raw: ## 4. Trackers
blocks.text: 4. Trackers

blocks.raw: A tracker is a tool used to track custom values over a specific period and set it as an eligibility criterion for upgrading the tier. Custom values can include bill amount, gross bill amount, points, line item price, and number of customer visits to the store.
blocks.text: A tracker is a tool used to track custom values over a specific period and set it as an eligibility criterion for upgrading the tier. Custom values can include bill amount, gross bill amount, points, line item price, and number of customer visits to the store.

blocks.raw: Up to three trackers can be defined for a tier upgrade.
blocks.text: Up to three trackers can be defined for a tier upgrade.

blocks.raw: You can use trackers for both individual customers and user groups. For individual upgrades, use customer-level tracker values. For group-based upgrades, use group-level tracker values, such as total group spend or group activity.
blocks.text: You can use trackers for both individual customers and user groups. For individual upgrades, use customer-level tracker values. For group-based upgrades, use group-level tracker values, such as total group spend or group activity.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 Note:
>
> To enable group-based tier upgrades, you must configure the SlabUpgrade activity for the User Group entity. Without this configuration, group-level upgrades will not be processed.
blocks.text: Note:To enable group-based tier upgrades, you must configure the SlabUpgrade activity for the User Group entity. Without this configuration, group-level upgrades will not be processed.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 Notes:
>
> * After tracker evaluation, you must configure the Transaction Point Allocation action. If you do not, users are upgraded one tier at a time and cannot skip tiers, even if tracker values qualify them for higher tiers. Tracker values are also scoped by the relevant Concept.
> * In the TransactionAdd flow, tracker evaluation runs before the current bill’s amount is recorded in the tracker’s aggregate. This means that on the transaction where a customer first crosses the tier threshold, the tracker may see a zero aggregate and the upgrade will not fire until the next transaction. To make the tier upgrade happen in the same transaction, add a 0-point transaction allocation action in a workflow set that executes before the tracker evaluation — this creates a PointsAward entry for the current bill and allows the tracker to include the current transaction’s value in its aggregate.
> * When a tier program is updated to include a tracker as an eligibility criterion, the tracker will only track the customer’s previous custom values for tier upgrades. For tier downgrades and renewals, the tracker will start monitoring custom values from the date it was configured in the tier program.

blocks.raw: # Creating upgrade criteria
blocks.text: Creating upgrade criteria

blocks.raw: You can create upgrade criteria for both individual customers and user groups. When setting up group-based criteria, ensure you use group-level tracker references and configure the SlabUpgrade activity for the User Group entity. This allows the system to evaluate group performance, such as total group spend, for tier upgrades.
blocks.text: You can create upgrade criteria for both individual customers and user groups. When setting up group-based criteria, ensure you use group-level tracker references and configure the SlabUpgrade activity for the User Group entity. This allows the system to evaluate group performance, such as total group spend, for tier upgrades.

blocks.raw: You can create dynamic upgrade criteria for tier upgrades by combining multiple criteria. You can define up to three eligibility criteria for a tier upgrade.
blocks.text: You can create dynamic upgrade criteria for tier upgrades by combining multiple criteria. You can define up to three eligibility criteria for a tier upgrade.

blocks.raw: Three types of logical operations can be placed between these criteria depending on the use case:
blocks.text: Three types of logical operations can be placed between these criteria depending on the use case:

blocks.raw: ## 1. Any (N-1) condition
blocks.text: 1. Any (N-1) condition

blocks.raw: The **Any (N-1)** operation can define the number of conditions required to qualify for a tier upgrade. When this operation is applied, the customer must meet the specified number of criteria to qualify for a tier upgrade.
blocks.text: The Any (N-1) operation can define the number of conditions required to qualify for a tier upgrade. When this operation is applied, the customer must meet the specified number of criteria to qualify for a tier upgrade.

blocks.raw: For example, assume there are 4 conditions/criteria defined in the eligibility criteria of the tier. Now, when the "ANY" is selected, the brand will have the following options:
blocks.text: For example, assume there are 4 conditions/criteria defined in the eligibility criteria of the tier. Now, when the "ANY" is selected, the brand will have the following options:

blocks.raw:
1. ANY 1
   1. This is just like a simple 'OR' condition. Among the 4 conditions, the user has to satisfy any 1 condition.
2. ANY 2
   1. Among the 4 conditions present, the user has to satisfy any 2 conditions.
3. ANY 3
   1. Among the 4 conditions present, the user has to satisfy any 3 conditions.
blocks.text: ANY 1This is just like a simple 'OR' condition. Among the 4 conditions, the user has to satisfy any 1 condition.ANY 2Among the 4 conditions present, the user has to satisfy any 2 conditions.ANY 3Among the 4 conditions present, the user has to satisfy any 3 conditions.

blocks.raw: **Note:** As per the above example, there is no "ANY 4". This is because, if the user has to follow all the 4 conditions that are present, then it is like "ALL 4". That is why, the ANY will have values till (N-1).

> 📘 Note
>
> For an **Any** condition, the upgrade type must be the same for all criteria. Selecting multiple upgrade types is not supported.
>
> This is primarily because, if different upgrade types are used in different conditions, in the event of success there is no way for the system to know "which condition's upgrade" criteria it should follow.

> Refer to the [types of tier upgrades](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/tier-upgrade#types-of-tier-upgrades) for more information.

blocks.raw:
> ❗️ Important
>
> All expressions are evaluated from left to right.\
> E.g.: The expression `A OR B AND C` is read as `(A OR B) AND C` as it is evaluated from left to right.
>
> It is recommended to use parentheses `()` and define the operators in full (`AND` or `OR`) or as (`&&` or `||`) when defining expressions to avoid ambiguity and ensure successful validation.
>
> Using a single `&` or `|` is invalid and unsupported.

blocks.text: Examples of tier upgrades

blocks.raw: ## 1. Any (N-1) condition
blocks.text: 1. Any (N-1) condition

blocks.raw: A brand has a travel rewards program that rewards customers and rewards a Platinum status for its most loyal customers. Platinum customers receive extra perks, such as larger discounts and access to premium partner hotels.
blocks.text: A brand has a travel rewards program that rewards customers and rewards a Platinum status for its most loyal customers. Platinum customers receive extra perks, such as larger discounts and access to premium partner hotels.

blocks.raw: The criteria for reaching Platinum status are as follows:
blocks.text: The criteria for reaching Platinum status are as follows:

blocks.raw:
* Earn **1500 lifetime points** by using the brand's services
* Take **5 flights** in the last **12 months**
* Stay in **3 partner hotels** in the last **12 months**
blocks.text: Earn 1500 lifetime points by using the brand's servicesTake 5 flights in the last 12 monthsStay in 3 partner hotels in the last 12 months

blocks.raw: The brand has set an **Any 1** condition for the tier upgrade. This means that if a customer meets any one of the above criteria, they will be upgraded to the Platinum tier.
blocks.text: The brand has set an Any 1 condition for the tier upgrade. This means that if a customer meets any one of the above criteria, they will be upgraded to the Platinum tier.

2. [Create or edit](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-a-multi-loyalty-program#getting-started) an existing loyalty program and [create the tiers](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-tiers-and-configure-tier-upgrade-conditions#creating-a-tier) if required.

blocks.raw: ## 3) Custom condition
blocks.text: 3) Custom condition

blocks.raw: An e-commerce site has a loyalty reward program that rewards regular users of the platform. The site offers a Plus status for its most loyal customers. Plus users receive extra perks, such as larger discounts and early access to sales.
blocks.text: An e-commerce site has a loyalty reward program that rewards regular users of the platform. The site offers a Plus status for its most loyal customers. Plus users receive extra perks, such as larger discounts and early access to sales.

blocks.raw: The criteria for reaching Plus status are as follows:
blocks.text: The criteria for reaching Plus status are as follows:

blocks.raw:
* Accumulate **3000 current points** (A)
* Make at least **5 purchases** in the last **6 months** (B)
* Spend over **$1000** in a single transaction (C)
blocks.text: Accumulate 3000 current points (A)Make at least 5 purchases in the last 6 months (B)Spend over $1000 in a single transaction (C)

blocks.raw: The brand has set a custom condition with the expression **`(A AND B) OR C`** for the tier upgrade. The customer must meet both conditions A and B or meet condition C to be eligible. This means that if a customer has accumulated 3000 points AND made five purchases in the last six months, OR if the customer has spent over $1000 in a single transaction, they will be upgraded to the Plus tier.

blocks.raw: To create a custom tier upgrade criteria, follow these steps:

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to **Home > Loyalty+** from the InTouch portal.
2. [Create or edit](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-a-multi-loyalty-program#getting-started) an existing loyalty program and [create the tiers](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-tiers-and-configure-tier-upgrade-conditions#creating-a-tier) if required.
3. [Create and configure](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/trackers-1#creating-trackers) all the required criteria trackers.

> ❗️ Important
>
> All expressions are evaluated from left to right.\
> For example, the expression `A OR B AND C` is read as `(A OR B) AND C` as it is evaluated from left to right.
>
> It is recommended to use parentheses `()` and define the operators in full (`AND` or `OR`) or as (`&&` or `||`) when defining expressions to avoid ambiguity and ensure successful validation.
>
> Using a single `&` or `|` is invalid and unsupported.

blocks.raw: In this case, there are three tiers in a loyalty program: Silver, Gold, and Diamond. The Silver tier awards 10% points for every transaction amount spent, Gold awards 20%, and Diamond awards 30%.
blocks.text: In this case, there are three tiers in a loyalty program: Silver, Gold, and Diamond. The Silver tier awards 10% points for every transaction amount spent, Gold awards 20%, and Diamond awards 30%.

blocks.raw: A customer is currently in the Gold tier with a lifetime purchase value of $14,000 and the criteria for upgrading to the Diamond tier is a lifetime purchase requirement of $15,000.
blocks.text: A customer is currently in the Gold tier with a lifetime purchase value of $14,000 and the criteria for upgrading to the Diamond tier is a lifetime purchase requirement of $15,000.

blocks.raw: The customer now makes a transaction of $2000.
blocks.text: The customer now makes a transaction of $2000.

blocks.raw: In this situation, you can award points to the customer in three ways:
blocks.text: In this situation, you can award points to the customer in three ways:

blocks.raw:
1. **Issue points and then upgrade to the next tier (Lazy):** Award points based on the current tier before upgrading. In this case, the customer receives the benefits of the Gold tier, which amounts to 20% of $2000, that is 400 points, and is then upgraded to the Diamond tier.
2. **Upgrade to the next tier and then issue points (Eager):** Upgrade the tier first, then award points based on the new tier. In this case, the customer is upgraded to the Diamond tier and is then rewarded with points equal to 30% of $2000 that is 600 points.
3. **Issue points, upgrade tier, and then issue remaining points (Dynamic):** Award points for the portion of the transaction that qualifies for the current tier, then upgrade the tier and award points for the remaining transaction amount. In this case, the customer earns 200 points for the initial $1000 transaction and then advances to the Diamond tier. Afterward, within the Diamond tier, the customer earns the remaining 300 points for the additional $1000 transaction amount.

blocks.raw:
<Callout icon="🚧" theme="warn">
  Notes

  * Impact on tier upgrades on returning a transaction: If a customer returns a transaction that resulted in a tier upgrade, the upgrade will be reversed, and the customer will be downgraded to the previous eligible tier.
  * If a tier upgrade action is added inside a Tracker ruleset, it overrides the intended upgrade type (Lazy, Eager, Dynamic) and forces the upgrade to occur before points allocation.
  * Restrictions on Bonus Issuance - Users with an INVALID email status are excluded from audience filters and ruleset execution for tier based bonuses.
  * Dynamic Slab Upgrade is only supported when the IndividualTracker is value-based, such as transaction amount or line-item amount. If you use points or AC trackers, the system does not split the source value for dynamic calculation. In these cases, all points are awarded at the current tier, and dynamic allocation across tiers does not occur.
  * Dynamic upgrade mode ties the tier upgrade to the transaction's point allocation step. If a transaction allocates zero points (for example, due to a workflow or promotion configuration issue), the tier upgrade will not fire either, even if the customer has met the eligibility criteria.
</Callout>
